Subjective: Ishidzu, a one and a half year old dog, presented with symptoms of head shaking and holding the head tilted to the left side for 2-3 days. The owner also reports decreased appetite during this period.
Objective: Physical examination revealed a foreign body in the left ear and yeast infection in the right ear. Ear cleaning was performed. The patient is currently receiving Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally.
Assessment: Foreign body in the left ear with concurrent yeast infection in the right ear causing otitis externa. Symptoms include head shaking, head tilt, and decreased appetite likely due to discomfort and infection.
Plan: Continue oral Cefpodoxime syrup for an additional 5-7 days. Administer Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days. Monitor response to treatment. If no improvement, perform ear swab culture and sensitivity testing to guide further therapy.
Conclusion: Otitis externa secondary to foreign body and yeast infection, under treatment with antibiotics and antifungal ear drops. Follow-up needed to assess resolution.
DifferentialDiagnosis: Other causes of head shaking and head tilt such as ear mites, bacterial otitis, neurological disorders, or vestibular disease should be considered if symptoms persist.
KeyIssues: Foreign body in left ear, yeast infection in right ear, head shaking, head tilt, decreased appetite.
AbnormalFindings: Foreign body in left ear canal, yeast growth in right ear canal, head tilt to left side.
CustomerInstructions: Administer prescribed Cefpodoxime syrup 3ml orally as directed for 5-7 more days. Apply Easotic ear drops once daily for 5 days. Avoid inserting objects into the ears. Monitor for improvement or worsening signs such as increased head shaking, discharge, or discomfort. Return for recheck or if no improvement after treatment course.
Protocols: Ear cleaning performed. Antibiotic therapy with Cefpodoxime syrup continued. Antifungal therapy with Easotic ear drops initiated. Culture and sensitivity planned if no response to treatment.
Reminders: Schedule follow-up appointment after completion of medication course. Consider ear swab culture if symptoms persist or worsen.
